## In a nutshell - Tax at source in Switzerland is withheld by the employer, not in both countries - From 1 January 2024, the exemptions change: €7,500 for old border guards, €10,000 for new ones - Old frontier workers: transitional regime until 2033 - The Italian tax credit in 730 avoids double taxation
## Key facts - **What**: Calculation of the tax at source on the Swiss border workers' paycheck - When: From 1 January 2024 (new agreement signed 23 December 2020) - Where: Ticino Canton, Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo passes and CH-Italy border - Who: Employed border workers working in Switzerland - Base rate: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% + AD/AC 1.1% + LAINF 0.7–1.5% + LPP 7–18% - Old-age exemption: €7,500 per year (transitory until 2033) - New exemption: €10,000 per year (permanent)
The tax at source in Switzerland affects the incomes of border workers who pass every day from the passes of Brogeda, Chiasso and Gaggiolo to reach the companies of Ticino and Lombardy. But how exactly is it calculated? And what was new about the new agreement ratified on 1 January 2024?
The tax is withheld directly by the employer and represents a percentage of your gross. Let's dispel a myth right away: it is not paid in both countries, but ONLY in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit, which you fill out in the EC framework of declaration 730.
The new December 2020 agreement (effective January 1, 2024) ### The Tax Credit Rule
This is where the Convention between Italy and Switzerland of 9 December 1976 comes into play, confirmed by the new agreement: you pay the tax ONLY in Switzerland. To avoid double taxation, Italy applies the tax credit. How does it work?
In your Italian 730, fill in the CE table reporting: the Swiss source tax actually paid during the year; the days of work in Switzerland; the gross income from cross-border work. The Revenue Agency calculates the credit based on the Italian rate you are entitled to (23%, 35% or 43% depending on your tier) and compares it with what you have already paid in Switzerland. If you have paid less, pay the difference; if you have paid more than due in Italy, you recover it as a credit. Refer to [nostra guida alla dichiarazione 730](nav:tax-return) for details on compiling the CE Framework.
Warning: this mechanism only works if your employer has correctly withheld the tax from you in Switzerland. If they did not do so by mistake, you are still liable to the Swiss tax authorities.

Here the novelty of 2024 is decisive. If you were already a border worker before 17 July 2023, you must apply: exemption of €7,500 per year (transitional regime until 2033). It means that the first part of your salary up to €7,500 is not subject to tax at source, the rest is normally calculated according to the rates. If you became frontier workers after that date:
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step 1: Gather your documents
From your December payslip (or your employer's annual statement), download: gross annual salary; withheld withholding tax (specific line item on the certificate); detailed OASI/IV/EO, ALV, UVG, BVG contributions; days of actual work (needed for the Italian tax return 'Modello 730').
### Step 2: Check the applied exemption
Ask your employer or your employer's tax advisor if the €7'500 (old cross-border commuters) or €10'000 (new cross-border commuters) exemption has been applied correctly. If you fall right on the border between the two regimes (which is rare), keep written confirmation of the date you officially became a cross-border worker. This document is required by the Italian tax authority in case of an audit.
### Step 3: Use the simulator
Access our [tax calculator](nav:calculator): enter your gross annual salary, select 'Ticino–Italy cross-border commuter', indicate the year (2026), and the system will show you the calculated withholding tax; detailed contributions for each item; estimated monthly net salary; amount to recover or pay in your '730' tax return.
### Step 4: Fill out the Italian 730 tax return
In Section CE ('quadro CE'), report the tax withheld from your Swiss payslip. If the amount is lower than the Italian tax due according to your tax bracket (23–43%), you pay the difference; if it is higher, you recover it as a tax credit in the same section.
### Step 5: Keep everything
Archive in a single folder: monthly payslips (originals or PDFs from the company portal); annual tax certificate (if provided by the employer); receipts of tax payments from Switzerland (available via ESTV or Swiss portal); submitted '730' tax return and receipt from the Italian Revenue Agency ('Agenzia delle Entrate').
### Who to contact
If the numbers do not add up or you have doubts: contact your employer (HR/payroll office) to check if the exemption is applied correctly; consult an Italian tax advisor for your '730' and tax credit; visit the FTA/ESTV website (estv.admin.ch) for details on Swiss taxes; check our [payslip simulator](nav:calculator) to verify calculations and the [border crossing comparator](nav:border-map) for waiting times at the borders. ## Key facts - **What**: Tax at source on income from employment - When: Effective from 1 January 2024 (New Frontier Agreement) - Where: Switzerland (withheld in paycheck); Italy (credit in 730) - Who: Border workers with G Permit (classified as old or new from 17 July 2023) - Amount: Deductible €7,500 (old border guards, 2024–2033) or €10,000 (new) - Entry into force: 1 January 2024, following signature 23 December 2020 - Basic Convention: Italy-Switzerland of 9 December 1976
The New Frontier Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and entered into force on 1 January 2024, has redesigned the rules of tax at source for those who cross the borders between Ticino and Italy on a daily basis. For the border worker who works in Switzerland and resides in Italy, the tax at source is withheld ONLY by the Swiss employer. It does not happen, contrary to what is sometimes believed, in both countries.
The Agreement between Italy and Switzerland, signed on 9 December 1976, provides that Switzerland has the exclusive right to tax the income from employment of those who reside in Italy but work in the territory ### How to calculate: Swiss rates and contributions
Tax at source in Switzerland is not a single tax, but an aggregate of contributions and taxes paid by the employee on the paycheck. The current federal rates are:

All these payments constitute the withholding tax that appears on the Swiss paycheck of the border worker. The calculation is crude: the gross salary is reduced by these contributions before any cantonal or municipal tax deduction. Switzerland, in fact, uses an early withholding system that extracts contributions directly and leaves the subject net of any further cantonal tax debts.

item.title: Permit Request G: complete step-by-step procedure
item.description: Practical guide to applying for the G Permit: the subjects involved, documents required, waiting times, and the tax and social security implications for the Ticino-Italy border crossing.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Permit G: work authorization for EU/EFTA nationals working in Switzerland and residing abroad - Procedure initiated by the Swiss employer at the cantonal office and SEM - Main documents: identity, employment contract, criminal certificate
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border work authorization in Switzerland - Who: Swiss employer, Canton Ticino Migration Office, SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) - Where: Ticino Migration Office (Bellinzona), SEM (Bern) - When: Administrative procedure, variable times per canton and season - Validity: Generally 5 years, renewable - Access: Italian and EU citizens, residing in Italy, with a concrete job offer in CH
### What is the G Permit and who requests it
The G Permit is the work authorization intended for Italian and European Union citizens who maintain residence in their country of origin (or in an EU state) and work in Switzerland. For the Ticino-Italy border crossing, the G Permit is the most common legal form: it allows you to cross the Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo or Ponte Tresa crossings daily to go to work, without moving to Switzerland.
Unlike Permit B (permanent residence in Switzerland), Permit G is a temporary solution linked to the specific employment relationship with a certain employer. There is no "Generic G Permit": it is always bound to a job with a defined contract. For ### Procedure step-by-step: from submission to release
Step 1: Submission of the application at the cantonal Ticino counter. The employer, or a HR consultant appointed, presents themselves at the migration counter with the complete file. The office checks the conformity of the documentation; if something is missing, it requires integrations and communicates the terms for the correct presentation.
**Step 2: Priority check.** The cantonal office checks if the job opening was opened before to Swiss citizens, EEA residents in Switzerland, or already active border workers G, or if it was reserved for the specific candidate for rare job. This check requires some working days and cannot be skipped.
Step 3: Transmission to SEM. Once the priority is confirmed, the file is forwarded to SEM for federal review. Here, administrative checks, security and anti-terrorism archive checks are carried out.
Step 4: Issuance and collection of the permit. If SEM approves, it communicates the release to the cantonal office of Ticino, which notifies the border worker. The permit can be collected at the counter within pre-established times.
Step 5: Automatic enrollment in Swiss pension systems. From the agreed day in the contract, the employer is responsible for enrolling the border worker in: cantonal AVS (first pillar), LPP company fund (second pillar), injury insurance (SUVA or private LAINF), and unemployment insurance (AD).
### Real times and variability of the procedure
Two to four weeks is the indicative time for a complete and correct application during low administrative season. If the documentation is incomplete, times are extended for integrations; if we are in peak season (May-September) or complex issues arise on priority, the procedure can last 2-3 months. The border worker should not wait passively: the employer should communicate the state of progress weekly, and at the cantonal office it is always possible to ask for information on times and any accelerated steps.
### Permit G vs Permit B: when to choose which
The Permit B (for residents) is suitable for those who decide to move to live in Switzerland. The Permit G is the solution for commuters: Italian residence, Swiss work.
From a tax point of view, the implications are significant. A border worker G pays the withholding tax directly on the Swiss income according to the New Border Agreement (in force from January 1, 2024, ratified by Italy with Law 83/2023). Italy avoids double taxation through a tax credit in the CE framework of the income tax return. A resident B pays in both countries, benefiting from the Convention against double taxation (December 9, 1976). [The choice of permit has significant repercussions on the wallet](nav:permit-compare).
### Implications for the border worker's pension and tax
Accepting a job as a border worker G entails mandatory Swiss payments: AVS (first pillar) 5.3% of the payroll, invalidity and death insurance (AI/IPG) included, unemployment insurance (AD) 1.1% on income up to CHF 148,200, injury insurance (LAINF) 0.7-1.5% at the employer's expense. The second pillar (LPP, pension fund) varies from 7-18% of the payroll according to age (the rates increase from the 25th year) and fund selected by the employer.
These payments remain credited and count towards the old-age pension. For older border workers (those who already had border worker status before July 17, 2023), a transitional regime applies until 2033 with a CHF 7,500 exemption on health tax. New border workers from 2024 onwards have a EUR 10,000 exemption according to the New Border Agreement.
The withholding tax is withheld ONLY in Switzerland, not in Italy. In the 730 declaration (or Redditi), the border worker declares the foreign work income; the tax credit in the CE framework compensates the Swiss withholding, preventing double taxation. At INPS, the border worker continues to pay separate management contributions if they have Italian autonomous income; otherwise, they are excluded from INPS as an employee (the main pension is AVS Swiss).
For a precise estimate of the net payroll and taxes, consult [the border worker calculator by entering gross salary, canton, and marital status](nav:calculator).
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Checklist before signing the contract
Before accepting a Swiss job offer, check that: (1) the employer is willing to handle the G Permit procedure (most do, but it's best to confirm); (2) the contract clearly specifies salary, hours, start date, workplace, and duration; (3) you possess a valid Italian passport or ID card; (4) you know which border crossing you will use daily (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa) and the average transit times.
### Documents to provide to the employer
Once the preliminary contract is signed, the employer will ask for: (1) a copy of your ID document; (2) a certificate of good conduct from your Italian municipality of residence; (3) your Italian bank IBAN; (4) your Italian address; (5) your phone number and email. Provide the documentation within the required timeframe: delays will block the presentation.
### Salary calculation and online simulation
The Swiss salary includes: agreed gross salary, AVS/AI/IPG deductions (~5.3%), unemployment insurance (1.1% on CHF 148'200), LAINF (0.7–1.5%, employer-paid), LPP (variable 7–18% based on age). For a net estimate, [simulate the salary by entering gross data, canton, and marital status](nav:payslip).
Regarding taxes: the withholding tax is deducted directly and paid by the employer. In Italy, complete the 730 declaration, reporting foreign income; the CE framework avoids double taxation. If you're a single employee with no other income, the 730 is straightforward.
### Entities to contact for doubts or delays
If the procedure is blocked: **Ticino Migration Office** (Department of Institutions and Territory, Bellinzona) for progress updates; SECO (Bern) for information on frontier legislation; SEM for federal review; CAF or Italian accountant for support with 730 declaration and tax credit.
### Practical tools available
Once employed, use: [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to verify your net salary every month; [comparator G Permit vs B](nav:permit-compare) to assess whether commuting is convenient; [CHF/EUR exchange tables](nav:exchange) if you manage accounts in different currencies; [guide to frontier meal vouchers](nav:ristorni) if you're entitled to tax recovery.
### From contract to first salary
The average time from contract signing to first salary is 4–8 weeks if everything proceeds smoothly. Don't wait passively: ask the employer for a weekly update. Once you acquire the G Permit, the 5-year renewal is simplified; you'll access pre-employment benefits (AVS, LPP, LAMal with option right) and frontier tax benefits, making this choice economically convenient for thousands of Italian workers in Ticino.
